title: Sagara's sons dig the earth in search of the ritual horse
introduction: The ritual horse released by Emperor Sagara is snatched away by Indra in order to cause hindrance to the ritual. The ritual cannot proceed to culmination without the horse. Then Sagara orders his sixty thousand sons to search for that horse, asking them to dig earth to trace it, if it is not found on earth. And the princes will dig earth when they have not found the horse on earth, to the grief of beings living in netherworlds.
closing: इति वाल्मीकिरामायणे आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे एकोनचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 39th chapter in Bala Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
विश्वामित्रवचः श्रुत्वा कथान्ते रघुनंदन |
उवाच परमप्रीतो मुनिं दीप्तमिवानलम्
verses.iast:
viśvāmitra vacaḥ śrutvā kathānte raghunandana |
uvāca parama prīto munim dīptam iva analam
verses.translation: On listening the narration of Vishvamitra, Rama, the delighter of Raghu's dynasty is highly rejoiced, and at the end of the episode he spoke to sage whose glow is fire like.

verses.devanagari:
श्रोतुमिच्छामि भद्रं ते विस्तरेण कथामिमाम् |
पूर्वजो मे कथं ब्रह्मन् यज्ञं वै समुपाहरत्
verses.iast:
śrotum icchāmi bhadram te vistareṇa kathām imām |
pūrvajo me katham brahman yaGYam vai samupāharat
verses.translation: "I am interested to listen this episode exhaustively, oh, Brahman, let good betide you, how my ancestor Sagara had completed the Vedic-ritual, really.

glosses.meaning: this, episode, extensively, to listen, I am interested
of mine, earlier, born one - my ancestor Sagara

verses.devanagari:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा कौतूहलसमन्वितः |
विश्वामित्रस्तु काकुत्स्थमुवाच प्रहसन्निव
श्रूयतां विस्तरो राम सगरस्य महात्मनः |
verses.iast:
tasya tat vacanam śrutvā kautūhala samanvitaḥ |
viśvāmitraḥ tu kākutstham uvāca prahasanniva
śrūyatām vistaro rāma sagarasya mahātmanaḥ |
verses.translation: On listening the words of Rama that are inclusive of his inquisitiveness, Sage Vishvamitra smilingly spoke to that descendent of Kakutstha, "oh, Rama, let the episode of the great-souled Sagara be listened vividly." Vishvamitra thus commenced to narrate that episode.

verses.devanagari:
शंकरश्वशुरो नाम हिमवानिति विश्रुतः
विंध्यपर्वतमासाद्य निरीक्षेते परस्परम् |
verses.iast:
śaṅkara śvaśuro nāma himavān iti viśrutaḥ
vindhya parvatam āsādya nirīkṣete parasparam |
verses.translation: "The father-in-law of god Shankara who is well-known by the name of Himavan sets eyes on Mt. Vindhya, which stands as loftily as Himalayas, and those two mountains peer at each other.

glosses.meaning: by name, thus, well, known vindhya parvatam aasaadya = Vindhya, mountain, [Himavan] attaining - by sight, set eyes on
without, wink [stares, peers] each other - Vindhya and Himalayas look at each other.

verses.devanagari:
तयोर्मध्ये प्रवृत्तोऽभूद्यज्ञः स पुरुषोत्तम
स हि देशो नरव्याघ्र प्रशस्तो यज्ञकर्मणि|
verses.iast:
tayor madhye sambhavat yaGYaḥ sa puruṣottama
sa hi deśo naravyāghra praśasto yaGYa karmaṇi |
verses.translation: "Oh, best one among men, Rama, that Vedic-ritual of Sagara came to pass in between those two mountains, namely Himalayas and Vindhya ranges, and oh, tigerly-man Rama, that area is renowned for Vedic-rituals, isn't it!

glosses.meaning: that, Vedic ritual o f Sagara
of them two - between Vindhya and Himalayas mountains between

verses.devanagari:
तस्याश्वचर्यां काकुत्स्थ दृढधन्वा महारथः
अंशुमानकरोत्तात सगरस्य मते स्थितः |
verses.iast:
tasya aśva caryām kākutstha dṛḍha dhanvā mahārathaḥ
aṃśumān akarot tāta sagarasya mate sthitaḥ |
verses.translation: "Oh, dear sire Rama, the grandson of Sagara and the son of exiled Asamanja is Amshuman, oh, descendant of Kakutstha, which Anshuman's bow will be unfaltering and who is a top-speeded chariot-rider, and he has escorted ritual-horse released.
notes: Details regarding the release of horse are at Bala Kanda 1-14-1

glosses.meaning: of horse, course of action - from release to retrieval

verses.devanagari:
तस्य पर्वणि तं यज्ञं यजमानस्य वासवः
राक्षसीं तनुमास्थाय यज्ञीयाश्वमपाहरत् |
verses.iast:
tasya parvaṇi tam yaGYam yajamānasya vāsavaḥ
rākṣasīm tanum āsthāya yaGYiya aśvam apāharat |
verses.translation: "And on the day of a sacred function called ukthyam , Indra assumed the form of a demon and stole the ritual horse of the chief of the ritual, namely Sagara.

glosses.meaning: at auspicious time [ukthya, the day of sacred function]

verses.devanagari:
ह्रियमाणे तु काकुत्स्थ तस्मिन्नश्वे महात्मनः
उपाध्यायगणाः सर्वे यजमानमथाब्रुवन् |
verses.iast:
hriyamāṇe tu kākutstha tasmin aśve mahātmanaḥ
upādhyāya gaṇāḥ sarve yajamānam atha abruvan |
verses.translation: "While that ritual-horse of the great-souled Sagara is stolen, all the congregations of the Ritviks, the religious-teachers, then spoke to the chief propitiator, namely Sagara.

glosses.meaning: then, all, religious-teachers', congregations - of ritwiks

verses.devanagari:
अयं पर्वणि वेगेन यज्ञियाश्वोऽपनीयते
हर्तारं जहि काकुत्स्थ हयश्चैवोपनीयताम् |
verses.iast:
ayam parvaṇi vegena yaGYiya aśvo apanīyate
hartāram jahi kākutstha hayaḥ ca eva upanīyatām |
verses.translation: " 'Oh, Sagara,the descendent of Kakutstha, at this auspicious time the ritual horse is hastily diverted, you kill him who stole the horse, and let that horse be fetched.

glosses.meaning: who stole it - horse's thief, you kill
horse, also, that way, be fetched.

verses.devanagari:
यज्ञश्च्छिद्रं भवत्येतत्सर्वेषामशिवाय नः
तत्तथा क्रियतां राजन् यज्ञोऽच्छिद्रः क्रतुर्भवेत् |
verses.iast:
yaGYaḥ cchidram bhavati etat sarveṣām aśivāya naḥ
tat tathā kriyatām rājan yaGYo acchidraḥ kruto bhavet |
verses.translation: " 'This hindrance in Vedic-ritual will become inauspicious for all of us, thereby, oh, king, action may be taken as to how there can be no fault in proceedings of the ritual.' The religious-teachers of Sagara have advised him in this way.

glosses.meaning: this one - the happening, in Vedic-ritual, hindrance
that way, action may be taken.

verses.devanagari:
सोऽपाध्यायवचः श्रुत्वा तस्मिन्सदसि पार्थिवः
षष्टिं पुत्रसहस्राणि वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह |
verses.iast:
so upādhyāya vacaḥ śrutvā tasmin sadasi pārthivaḥ
ṣaṣṭim putra sahasrāṇi vākyam etat uvāca ha |
verses.translation: "On hearing the words of religious-teachers that king Sagara indeed spoke this much to his sixty thousand sons in that religious-council.

glosses.meaning: he Sagara, religious-teachers, words, on hearing
this much, sentence, spoke to, indeed.

verses.devanagari:
गतिं पुत्रा न पश्यामि रक्षसां पुरुषर्षभाः
मंत्रपूतैर्महाभागैरास्थितो हि महाक्रतुः |
verses.iast:
gatim putrā na paśyāmi rakṣasām puruṣarṣabhāḥ
mantra pūtaiḥ mahābhāgaiḥ āsthito hi mahākratuḥ |
verses.translation: " 'Oh, sons, I do not envisage any way in for demons into this ritual, since oh, best ones among men, holy-sanctifiers who themselves are sanctified by the Vedic-hymns are conducting this glorious Vedic-ritual, isn't it.

glosses.meaning: for demons, approaching [here,] not, I envisage
by hymns, sanctified, by holy, sanctifiers
presided over - being conducted, isn't it.

verses.devanagari:
तद्गच्छत विचिन्वध्वं पुत्रका भद्रमस्तु वः
समुद्रमालिनीं सर्वां पृथिवीमनुगच्छत |
verses.iast:
tat gacchata vicinvadhvam putrakā bhadram astu vaḥ
samudra mālinīm sarvām pṛthivīm anugacchata |
verses.translation: " 'Oh, sons, you may therefore proceed to search for the horse and its thief on entire earth as far as it is garlanded by the ocean, and safety betides you all.

glosses.meaning: for the purpose of searching - horse and its thief
to you all, safety, there will be
with ocean, garlanded - encompassed by oceans

verses.devanagari:
एकैकं योजनं पुत्रा विस्तारमभिगच्छत
यावत्तुरगसंदर्शस्तावत्खनत मेदिनीम् |
तमेव हयहर्तारं मार्गमाणा ममाज्ञया
verses.iast:
eka ekam yojanam putrā vistāram abhigacchata
yāvat turaga sandarśaḥ tāvat khanata medinīm |
tam eva haya hartāram mārgamāṇā mama āGYayā
verses.translation: " 'Oh, sons, let each prince advance searching one square yojana of earth, by my order you dig up the earth until the appearance of the horse, while searching for the stealer of that horse.

glosses.meaning: one [each prince,] one, yojana - area of earth
square area, you advance - allocate for yourself
till then, earth, you dig out.

verses.devanagari:
दीक्षितः पौत्रसहितः सोपाध्यायगणस्त्वहम् |
इह स्थास्यामि भद्रं वो यावत्तुरगदर्शनम्
verses.iast:
dīkṣitaḥ pautra sahitaḥ sa upādhyāya gaṇaḥ tu aham |
iha sthāsyāmi bhadram vo yāvat turaga darśanam
verses.translation: " 'As for myself, I will stay here only along with my grandson, namely Amsuman, and with the congregation of religious-teachers till the horse appears, as I am under vow of the ritual.' Thus Sagara instructed to his sixty thousand sons and stayed back at the ritual place.

glosses.meaning: under vow, I, for my part

verses.devanagari:
ते सर्वे हृष्टमनसो राजपुत्रा महाबलाः |
जग्मुर्महीतलं राम पितुर्वचनयंत्रिताः
verses.iast:
te sarve hṛṣṭamanaso rāja putrā mahābalāḥ |
jagmur mahī talam rāma pitur vacana yantritāḥ
verses.translation: "Animated by their father's words those great-mighty princes enthusiastically proceeded onto earth's surface in the preliminary round of search.

glosses.meaning: thus, who are addressed - the sons]

verses.devanagari:
गत्वा तु पृथिवीं सर्वमदृष्टा तं महबलाः |
योजनायामविस्तारमेकैको धरणीतलम् |
बिभिदुः पुरुषव्याघ्र वज्रस्पर्शसमैर्भुजैः
verses.iast:
gatva tu pṛthivīm sarvam adṛṣṭā tam mahabalāḥ |
yojanāyām avistāram ekaiko dharaṇī talam |
bibhiduḥ puruṣavyāghra vajra sparśa samaiḥ bhujaiḥ
verses.translation: "But, oh, tigerly-man Rama, on going round the earth in its entirety those great-mighty princes did not find that horse, then as said by their father they mapped the earth to a unit of one square yojana for each of them, and each of them hollowed out each and every area on the surface of earth with their arms that have the touch of the diamonds.

verses.devanagari:
शूलैरशनिकल्पैश्च हलैश्चापि सुदारुणैः |
भिद्यमाना वसुमती ननाद रघुनंदन
verses.iast:
śūlaiḥ aśani kalpaiḥ ca halaiḥ ca api sudāruṇaiḥ |
bhidyamānā vasumatī nanāda raghunandana
verses.translation: "Mother Earth bewailed while she is ruptured with spears also that are similar to thunderbolts, besides with very gruelling ploughs.

glosses.meaning: very, gruelling, with ploughs, also, even

verses.devanagari:
नागानां वध्यमानानामसुराणां च राघव |
राक्षसानां च दुर्धर्षः सत्त्वानां निनदोऽभवत्
verses.iast:
nāgānām vadhyamānānām asurāṇām ca rāghava |
rākṣasānām ca durdharṣaḥ sattvānām ninado abhavat
verses.translation: "Oh, Raghava, there emerged an unbearable rumpus from the serpents, asura-s, demons, and other beings living underneath the surface of earth, while they are killed during hollowing the earth.

glosses.meaning: being killed [while being battered,] of serpents

verses.devanagari:
योजनानां सहस्राणि षष्टिं तु रघुनंदन |
बिभिदुर्धरणीं राम रसातलमनुत्तमम्
verses.iast:
yojanānām sahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭim tu raghunandana |
bibhidur dharaṇīm rāma rasā talam anuttamam
verses.translation: "Oh, Rama, the legatee of Raghu's dynasty, thus sixty thousand square yojana-s of the earth is dug over, so as to make the earth's outermost plane as the unsurpassed rasaa tala, the sixth subterranean and the nethermost plane.

verses.devanagari:
एवं पर्वतसंबाधं जम्बूद्वीपं नृपात्मजाः |
खनन्तो नृपशार्दूल सर्वतः परिचक्रमुः
verses.iast:
evam parvata sambādham jambū dvīpam nṛpātmajāḥ |
khananto nṛpaśārdūla sarvataḥ paricakramuḥ
verses.translation: "Oh, the kingly tiger Rama, the sons of Sagara have endeavoured everywhere digging over the Jambu Island which is verily congested with mountains in this way.
notes: The jambu dvīpa is a continent according to Hindu mythology where the total continents listed are seven. "letter-spacing: 1.5pt; line-height : 115%; margin-top: 1%; margin-bottom: 1%">jambuu plakShaahya dviipau shaalmaliH ca aparo dvija | kushaH krauncaH tathaa shakaH puShkaraH ca eva ca saptamaH the seven continents are jambu- plakśa - śālmali- kuśa - kraunca - śāka - puṣkara, and jambu dvīpa is one among them.

verses.devanagari:
ततो देवाः सगंधर्वाः सासुराः सहपन्नगाः |
संभ्रांतमनसः सर्वे पितामहमुपागमन्
verses.iast:
tato devāḥ sa gandharvāḥ sa asurāḥ saha pannagāḥ |
sambhrānta manasaḥ sarve pitāmaham upāgaman
verses.translation: "All the gods along with gandharva-s, asura-s, and reptiles who are distraught at heart for the plight of earth have approached the Forefather, Brahma.

glosses.meaning: all are, distraught, at heart - for the plight of earth

verses.devanagari:
ते प्रसाद्य महात्मानं विषण्णवदनास्तदा |
ऊचुः परमसंत्रस्ताः पितामहमिदं वचः
verses.iast:
te prasādya mahātmānam viṣaṇṇa vadanāḥ tadā |
ūcuḥ parama santrastāḥ pitāmaham idam vacaḥ
verses.translation: "They the gods who are very highly scared, and who are chap-fallen, then spoke this sentence to the great-souled Forefather Brahma on gaining his grace.

glosses.meaning: of great-souled, Forefather - Brahma, getting the grace of

verses.devanagari:
भगवन् पृथिवी सर्वा खन्यते सगरात्मजैः |
बहवश्च महात्मानो वध्यन्ते जलचारिणः
verses.iast:
bhagavan pṛthivī sarvā khanyate sagara ātmajaiḥ |
bahavaḥ ca mahātmāno vadhyante jala cāriṇaḥ
verses.translation: " 'Oh, god Brahma, the sons of Sagara are digging entire earth, thus aquatic beings and many great-souls are being destroyed.

glosses.meaning: water, moving [aquatic beings, dwellers in netherworlds]
many, great souled beings, also, are being destroyed.

verses.devanagari:
अयं यज्ञ हरोऽस्माकमनेनाश्वोऽपनीयते |
इति ते सर्वभूतानि हिंसन्ति सगरात्मजाः
verses.iast:
ayam yaGYa haro asmākam anena aśvo apanīyate |
iti te sarva bhūtāni hiṃsanti sagara ātmajaḥ
verses.translation: " 'This one is the destroyer of our ritual... this one has carried off our ritual horse...' thinking thus and suspecting everyone those sons of Sagara are torturing all the living beings.' Thus all the gods have appealed to Brahma." So said Sage Vishvamitra to Rama and others.

glosses.meaning: all, living beings, they are torturing.
